hook: She reigned for 63 years, and gave her name to an age.

pages.x: Victoria was born at Kensington Palace in 1819. Her father died when she was eight months old. Her mother raised her under strict rules: she was never left alone, and slept in her mother's room until she became queen.
At six in the morning on 20 June 1837 she was woken to be told that her uncle, the king, was dead, and that she was queen. That same day she had her bed moved out of her mother's room.

In 1840 she married her German cousin, Prince Albert. As queen, she was the one who proposed. They had nine children, who married into the royal families of Europe, so she became "the grandmother of Europe".
In 1853 she was given chloroform to ease the pain of giving birth to her eighth child. She called it "blessed chloroform", and pain relief in childbirth soon became accepted.
Albert died in 1861. Victoria wore black for the remaining 40 years of her life, and hid from the public for years. Every morning his clothes were laid out, as if he were still alive.
"We are not amused" is her most famous line, but there is no proof she ever said it, and her diaries show she laughed a lot. In old age an Indian servant, Abdul Karim, taught her Hindustani.
In 1876 she was made Empress of India. By the end of her reign the British Empire covered about a fifth of the world's land: an empire on which the sun never set.
In 1897 she celebrated 60 years on the throne. When she died in 1901 she had reigned for 63 years, longer than any British monarch before her.
Her reign gave its name to the Victorian age, of railways, factories, a vast empire and strict manners.
pts: Ruled an empire on which the sun never set
Her children married into royal families all over Europe
